title: MLX Benchmark Result
description: Structured result envelope for a single benchmark suite run. Backwards-compatible v1 — optional fields may be added without bumping schema_version; breaking changes bump the version and change $id.
$comment: v1 additive fields (no version bump): top-level env_class, concurrency, reasoning_effort, serving; system.topology for multi-node cluster runs. 2026-07-27: results[].total_tokens_per_second is now the headline throughput metric (cumulative prompt+completion tok/s) — decode_tokens_per_second and prompt_tokens_per_second remain as supporting detail; no field added or removed, descriptions updated only.

schema_version.description: Schema version — bump when making breaking changes

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the run started

git_sha.description: Full or short git commit SHA of the repo at run time

pr_number.description: Pull request number if trigger is 'pr', otherwise null

model.description: Model name/ID used for inference (e.g. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-4bit)

model_revision.description: HuggingFace revision (tag or commit SHA) pinned at inference time

quantization.description: Quantization scheme as reported by the runtime (e.g. mlx-4bit, mxfp4, mxfp8)

campaign.description: Optional immutable campaign and cell identity for a coordinated local benchmark run.

cell_status.description: Protocol status for this cell. Only success rows carry scored benchmark metrics.

context.description: Context dimensions kept separate so configured capacity is never confused with actual prompt length.

skipped.description: True when the suite was skipped (e.g. MLX server unavailable on standard runner)

seed.description: RNG seed used for generation (when applicable)

gen_kwargs.description: Generation hyperparameters as passed to the inference API

env_class.description: Machine load class during the run: 'isolated' (nothing else contending for the box) or 'under-load' (other significant workloads present). Verdict policy gate 3 requires distinguishing these.

concurrency.description: Number of in-flight requests the run drove concurrently. 1 for serial runs; higher values contend and depress per-request throughput.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning/thinking effort the run asked the model for, verbatim as sent (e.g. 'low', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max', 'off'). Declared by the caller — a harness cannot observe a serving default or an agent CLI's own config. 'unstated' when no level was declared: absent is NOT the same as off, and a plausible guess here is indistinguishable from a measurement. Deliberately not an enum, because each model family names its own levels and rewriting one into another merges arms that are not the same arm.

serving.description: Identity of the inference server the run targeted

endpoint_port.description: TCP port the OpenAI-compatible endpoint listened on

served_model.description: Model id as advertised by the endpoint (may differ from 'model')

hostname.description: Short host label of the machine that ran the benchmark — distinguishes machines with identical chip/memory (e.g. a Mac Studio vs a MacBook Pro)

runner.description: GitHub Actions runner label (e.g. macos-latest, self-hosted)

topology.description: Multi-node cluster topology when the run spanned more than one machine (e.g. a two-Mac TB5 pipeline). Absent for single-node runs.

world_size.description: Total number of nodes participating in the run

parallelism.description: How the model was split across nodes

duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock duration attributed to this result (first-class, replacing tags.total_eval_time_s for new runs)

prompt_tokens_per_second.description: Aggregate prompt (prefill) throughput for this result: sum of prompt tokens across all samples divided by duration_seconds. Optional — populated when sample-level token counts are recoverable (e.g. lm-eval --log_samples + tokenizer).

decode_tokens_per_second.description: Aggregate decode (completion) throughput: sum of response tokens divided by duration_seconds. Supporting detail, not the headline number — a decode-only rate hides prefill-engine improvements entirely, even though a faster prefill is a real, felt latency win for any non-trivial prompt. See total_tokens_per_second for the headline metric.

total_tokens_per_second.description: PRIMARY / headline throughput metric: aggregate end-to-end (cumulative) throughput, (prompt + response) tokens divided by duration_seconds. Counts prefill and decode toward the same number because both are real time a caller waits on — a model with a much faster prefill and identical decode speed is genuinely faster in practice, and this is the field that reflects it. Prefer this over decode_tokens_per_second when reporting or comparing models.

first_token_latency_ms.description: Time to first token in milliseconds for this result (when measurable — typically populated by streaming-aware harnesses, left unset for lm-eval runs).

peak_rss_mb.description: Peak resident set size observed during this result, in megabytes. Complements memory_snapshots when per-result granularity is available.

tags.description: Arbitrary string key-value metadata (e.g. framework, output_tokens)

raw.description: Original unmodified output from the underlying tool or script

memory_snapshots.description: Memory usage measurements at different phases of the run

errors.description: Non-fatal errors or warnings encountered during the run
